title: Regenerate 7 Pilobolus narrations that Batch produced in the wrong voice
description:
Downstream cleanup for auritus-d84350. Filed on the Auritus board rather than PILO because PILO is a newsroom/editorial board (idea/assignment/research/... statuses) and rejects engineering tasks.

Pilobol.us narration was pinned to voice_id=serious, tts_backend=fish (Pilobol.us commit 7fc6a75, live on all 11 pages). 11 jobs minted. Jobs claimed by AWS Batch were narrated in the bundled stock voice, NOT 'serious', because the Batch image has no reference voices and Fish silently falls back (see auritus-d84350).

STATE AS OF 2026-10-03 ~12:15 ET
  5 done    batch  -> WRONG VOICE
  2 claimed batch  -> WILL BE WRONG VOICE
  1 done    local  -> correct ('serious' via 8-bit MLX)
  3 pending        -> whichever worker claims first

Job hashes: 678e800a a2085dd3 1ff2b869 2c71ccf0 5a32f11f 6cb29cb1 468ace02 cae1f4db 1039b796 2835f0b1 da9b4710
Inspect: curl -H 'x-auritus-site-key: WuNsWJc9fLoFesPzXkg2BZBurubafE2F' https://4o6atlkpeh.execute-api.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/jobs/<hash>
NOTE the site key must be a HEADER; ?site_key= returns 'site_key_required'.

WHY BATCH GOT THEM
Minted ~2.5h before login completed, so the 15-min local-claim timeout expired and Step Functions fell back to Batch GPU. Modelled cost that day: $2.34 GPU, $0.003 platform, $0.00 avoided.

NEXT STEPS - Ryan deferred this decision, confirm scope before acting
1. Regenerate all 11 for a uniform voice+model, or only the Batch ones? Batch uses full-precision fishaudio/s2-pro, local uses 8-bit MLX, so a mixed set will not sound uniform even after the voice bug is fixed.
2. Start the local worker BEFORE minting, or inside the 15-min window, so Batch never claims. Run it from /Users/home/Projects/Auritus - the worker derives voices_dir from its own config relative to cwd, overriding AURITUS_VOICES.
3. 'auritus job regenerate --hash <h>' exists. There is no 'job create' - jobs are minted only by a browser loading a page under the origin-locked site key (Pilobol.us has puppeteer for this).
4. Login is 'auritus login --sso google'. Bare 'auritus login' prompts for email/password and will not work with Google auth.
5. Fish MLX weights (6.3 GB) already downloaded on this machine.

Verify by LISTENING. status=done does not mean the voice is correct - that is exactly what auritus-d84350 is about.

comments.author: home
comments.text:
Regeneration complete 2026-10-03. Scope corrected: Batch had produced 10 of 11 narrations, not 7 (the 3 pending ones were later claimed by Batch). All 10 were regenerated on the local worker (8-bit MLX Fish, voice_id=serious, tts_backend=fish, voices dir /Users/home/Projects/Auritus/voices, code at develop incl. PR #77 fail-loudly). cae1f4db (the correct local one) was not touched; its audio hash is unchanged.

Voice check: speaker embeddings (resemblyzer) of each full file, cosine similarity to (A) the known-correct local narration cae1f4db and (S) the stock basic_ref_en.wav. Before regeneration every Batch file was closer to stock than to correct (A 0.80-0.83, S 0.83-0.88). After, every file is far closer to correct (A 0.95-0.98, S 0.66-0.70). Worker log shows each job claimed by local:BlackbookM1 with backend=fish and Completed; the serious reference had to resolve or the job fails loudly.

Live serving: pages embed aurit.us/embed.js with the site key and ask the API for the job's audio_url, so the job record is what readers get. Fresh downloads via the API for all 10 are byte-identical (sha256 prefix) to the regenerated files and differ from the before files. Pilobol.us was not modified.

Anomalies:
1. 6cb29cb1 was the longest (about 36 min locally, 151 MB). Its record now shows worker_type=batch, claimed 19:47:02Z, completed 19:54:27Z, 445s, so the Batch fallback claimed it while the local worker was still generating (well past the 15 min window, despite the local claim). The S3 object was last written 19:53:45Z, and its bytes are in the serious voice (0.978 to correct, 0.693 to stock), so the served audio is the local one. The record's producer is wrong and some Batch GPU spend was incurred. Worth a follow-up: Step Functions fallback should not take a job with a live local heartbeat; and a Batch mark_done should not overwrite a local completion.
2. Starting the stock worker claimed an unrelated stale pending demo job (139c884e, f5 backend, Sept) before I killed it. I released it with job retry --force; it is pending again. The remaining regeneration ran through the stock daemon code with the claimable list filtered to the 10 target hashes.
3. The CLI refreshes tokens automatically from the refresh token; no session expiry occurred.
